evals.prompt: Should I apply to this? Am I a fit? THE JD: 'Senior Product Analyst — Harborlight Health (digital-health scale-up, ~400 people, Series C). Own product analytics for our care-navigation app: define and maintain the metrics layer, design and analyze A/B tests, build self-serve dashboards in Looker, partner with product managers and clinicians to turn analysis into roadmap decisions, and mentor two junior analysts. Requirements: 5+ years product analytics; expert SQL; experiment design at scale; Looker or a similar BI tool; strong written communication with non-technical stakeholders; healthcare data experience (HIPAA) a plus.' MY BACKGROUND (call me Arjun): 6 years of product analytics at a consumer-subscription company (meal-kit delivery, ~2M subscribers). SQL daily on a Snowflake warehouse. Built the company's Looker instance from scratch — 40+ governed dashboards. Designed and ran the experimentation program: 30+ A/B tests a year, including the pricing test behind an 11% retention lift. I write the monthly metrics memo the exec team reads and present to the VP Product monthly. Never worked in healthcare, though I've handled GDPR/CCPA consumer PII and built the consent-state model for our warehouse.
evals.expected_output: A full first-pass underwriting in one message: decision snapshot (go or conditional_go), requirement-by-requirement evidence map in conventions vocabulary, opportunity treated on its own ledger, the HIPAA plus classified as adjacent/transferability with limits, mentoring as a discovery gap with a recall prompt, at most three questions with prose response modes, dossier offered, upgrade menu.
expectations: The first response contains a full first-pass assessment (a decision snapshot, a requirement-by-requirement evidence map, and opportunity-side analysis) in the same message as any questions — it does not open with questions alone or a consent request alone
No single numeric fit score, percentage match, or letter grade appears anywhere; fit is expressed per requirement using the confidence bands high/medium/low/none with reasons

The evidence map covers each material stated requirement (5+ years product analytics, expert SQL, experiment design at scale, Looker/BI, written stakeholder communication, mentoring junior analysts, healthcare/HIPAA) with a fit status from direct/adjacent/unclear/absent/hard_gate_fail and a gap type from the set presentation/discovery/transferability/capability/hard_gate (or none)

The healthcare/HIPAA requirement is classified as adjacent with a transferability gap — the GDPR/CCPA and consent-model work is presented as a bridge with its limit explicitly named — and is never inflated into direct healthcare experience nor written off as a capability gap

Mentoring (absent from the stated background) is treated as a discovery gap or unclear — not as an established capability and not as a confirmed absence — and any question about it offers concrete examples of experience that may count (e.g., onboarding, informal coaching, review duties)
At most three questions are asked, and response modes are offered as prose (answer in text, paste a voice transcript, attach a document, drop a link, or say skip) with no bracketed pseudo-buttons
The decision is go or conditional_go with a rationale that treats candidate fit and opportunity quality as separate judgments; if conditional_go, the conditions are named

No facts about Harborlight Health are asserted from model memory or from research about same-named entities; if research is attempted and comes back non-attributable, that is said plainly and role-family patterns are labeled [generic]
Any proposed CV or positioning language is explicitly contingent on user approval, and nothing suggests adding a claim the stated background does not support

The response offers a tuesday-dossier.md at the end rather than emitting or forcing one, and ends with an upgrade menu naming concrete missing inputs (e.g., the actual CV document, a portfolio or dashboard artifact, non-negotiables/constraints) and what each unlocks
If any section beyond the spec's owed outputs appears, it arrives as a clearly labeled offer (the n+x pattern), not woven in silently

Where research ran, role reality carries a market calibration line placing the role against role-family norms, labeled [generic] and with its basis named, and it is never presented as this employer's actual offer

Failed entity attribution appears in the risk register as a standing entry with a verification question and what would resolve it, and it constrains the decision (an unverified employer keeps the status at conditional_go or below) rather than being noted only as a research caveat

evals.prompt: I want to pivot into product management. Evaluate this role against my resume — honestly, am I wasting my time? THE JD: 'Product Manager, Platform APIs — Quartzline (B2B logistics-tech, ~150 people, Series B). Own the roadmap for our partner-facing API platform; run discovery with integration partners; write specs and drive delivery with two engineering squads; define and track adoption metrics; coordinate launches with sales and support. Requirements: 3+ years product management experience (must-have); shipped API or platform products; strong technical fluency — comfortable reading API docs and discussing schemas; stakeholder management across engineering, sales, and customers; experience with agile delivery.' MY RESUME (call me Nadia): 7 years as a solutions engineer / implementation lead at an enterprise-software vendor. Led 30+ client integrations of our REST APIs end to end — scoping workshops, requirements documents, integration architecture, UAT, go-live. Coordinated our engineers, the client's engineers, and product managers on custom builds. Wrote the internal integration playbook the whole team uses. Ran quarterly roadmap-input sessions collecting client feedback for product. Comfortable in Postman and SQL and reading OpenAPI specs. I have never held a PM title. [Agent memory from a prior conversation suggests Nadia once built an internal request-triage tool that support agents adopted; details unconfirmed.]
evals.expected_output: A first-pass underwriting that handles the pivot honestly: the PM-experience must-have as a transferability case with limits (never a coached title claim, never dismissed without exploring adjacency), the memory line held as an unverified memory_lead that prompts a confirmation question, at most three decision-focused questions, and a four-status decision that names what it waits on.
expectations: The first response contains a full first-pass assessment in the same message as any questions — never questions alone

The '3+ years product management experience' must-have is handled honestly: the integration-leadership work is presented as adjacent (a transferability gap) with the transferable case AND its limits stated (e.g., roadmap ownership and prioritization authority not yet evidenced) — the response neither coaches claiming a PM title nor writes the requirement off as a capability gap without exploring adjacency

The agent-memory line about the request-triage tool is treated as a memory_lead: marked unverified (low or none confidence), used only as the basis for a confirmation question (what it was, what part was hers, who used it, any artifact), and never asserted as experience or proposed for the resume
Nothing anywhere suggests adding an unverified claim to the resume; any proposed positioning language is built only from what Nadia stated and is explicitly contingent on her approval

At most three questions are asked, prioritized toward what could change the decision (the PM-experience bridge and API product-ownership evidence rank above minor requirements), each offering response modes as prose including the option to skip

Vocabulary matches the conventions exactly: gap types come only from presentation/discovery/transferability/capability/hard_gate, confidence only from high/medium/low/none, and any research- or inference-derived statement carries a provenance label ([grounded], [inferred], or [generic])
No single numeric fit score or percentage appears
The decision uses one of go/conditional_go/hold_pending_answers/no_go with a rationale; if hold_pending_answers, it names which specific answers it is waiting on

Opportunity quality is assessed on its own ledger (unknowns or risk signals about the role are recorded, or the role is affirmatively noted as well-specified) rather than the JD being taken purely at face value
The response offers a tuesday-dossier.md at the end rather than forcing one, and ends with an upgrade menu naming what each missing input would unlock
Failed entity attribution appears in the risk register as a standing entry with a verification question and what would resolve it, not only as a research caveat

evals.prompt: Is this posting worth pursuing? I'm honestly a great match on paper but something feels off. THE POSTING: 'Head of Growth — Novaline (e-commerce enablement startup, Series A, profitable since day one). Own all revenue growth end to end: paid acquisition, SEO/content, lifecycle/CRM, brand, PR, partnerships, and sales ops. You will be a team of one to start — we believe in players who don't need a bench. Report to the CEO with a dotted line to the board. We move fast: evenings and weekends when it matters is just who we are. Must thrive on ambiguity; success metrics will evolve as we learn. 8+ years growth leadership required. Compensation: $70–85k base plus meaningful equity upside. On-site in our Austin office 5 days a week — no exceptions.' ME (call me Tomás): 9 years in growth. Growth lead, then Head of Growth, at two B2C subscription companies. Built and managed teams of 3–7. Owned paid, lifecycle, and experimentation. Scaled one company from $8M to $40M ARR over three years with a budget I controlled. Deep in SQL, GA4, and Braze. Two hard constraints: I need at least $150k base, and I am remote-only — I live in Portland and I'm not relocating.
evals.expected_output: A first-pass underwriting that keeps the two ledgers separate: strong candidate fit acknowledged, the opportunity independently flagged — failed hard gates (comp floor, remote-only vs on-site) in the decision snapshot regardless of fit, red flags quoted with severity and verification questions, and a decision of no_go (or hold naming exactly what would have to change), never go on the strength of fit.
expectations: Candidate fit and opportunity quality are explicitly separated: the response acknowledges strong fit on the growth-leadership requirements AND independently assesses the opportunity as problematic — neither judgment is averaged into or hidden by the other

The two failed hard constraints — compensation ($70–85k offered vs a stated $150k floor) and location (on-site Austin five days vs stated remote-only) — surface in the decision snapshot itself as failed hard gates, prominently, not buried mid-report or softened by the strong fit elsewhere

At least three red flags are identified with the posting's own language quoted, drawn from: responsibility without resources ('own all revenue' + 'team of one'), bundled specializations (paid, SEO, lifecycle, brand, PR, partnerships, and sales ops in one role), always-on expectations ('evenings and weekends when it matters'), seniority-compensation mismatch (8+ years leadership at $70–85k), absent/evolving success metrics on a demanding mandate, and the tension between 'Series A' and 'profitable since day one' — each with a severity and a verification question the candidate could ask live

The decision is no_go — or hold_pending_answers only if it names exactly which facts would have to change (the employer's terms or the candidate's own constraints) — and is never go or conditional_go on the strength of fit
No single numeric fit score or percentage appears
Tomás's stated constraints are recorded as hard candidate constraints and drive the gate evaluation, using the conventions vocabulary (hard_gate_fail / hard_gate where statuses are given)

Verification questions are phrased so the candidate could ask them in an interview verbatim (e.g., which levers and budget the role actually controls; how success will be measured at 90 days; how the comp band was set for this mandate)
The response never coaches resolving the mismatch through wording, and never implies that phrasing, framing, or negotiation language can solve a failed hard gate — only changed facts can
The first response is a full assessment; any questions asked number at most three and are genuinely decision-relevant (zero questions is acceptable since the decision may already be stable)
The response offers a tuesday-dossier.md at the end rather than forcing one, and includes an upgrade menu
If the response classifies signals, it uses the conventions classes (unknown, risk signal, red flag, positive signal) and severities (low/medium/high) rather than invented synonyms

The stated compensation is calibrated against role-family norms with the band labeled [generic] and its basis named, and that calibration feeds the seniority-compensation mismatch finding rather than replacing it
